study.price_basis_note: Stock returns use DailyPriceBar.close; benchmark returns use BenchmarkPriceBar.close -- in both cases only rows whose price_basis is SPLIT_ADJUSTED (AS_TRADED rows are never read by research). The SPLIT_ADJUSTED rows come from Massive's daily-aggregate request with adjusted=true, which (per Polygon's own aggregates contract, which Massive -- formerly Polygon.io -- uses as-is) means split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted and not total-return. So both series are split-adjusted price series; cash dividends are excluded from both. DailyPriceBar.adjusted_close stays unconditionally NULL under the current ingestion path and must not be read as a further adjustment on top of close; BenchmarkPriceBar has no adjusted-level column at all. These are therefore split-adjusted price returns, dividends excluded -- not dividend-reinvested total returns. The abnormal return is a simple market-adjusted figure (stock return minus benchmark return, implicit beta of 1) -- it is not a CAPM alpha, a factor alpha, or a regression-based excess return.

The SPLIT_ADJUSTED rows come from Massive's daily-aggregate request with adjusted=true, which (per Polygon's own aggregates contract, which Massive -- formerly Polygon.io -- uses as-is) means split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted and not total-return. So both series are split-adjusted price series; cash dividends are excluded from both. DailyPriceBar.adjusted_close stays unconditionally NULL under the current ingestion path and must not be read as a further adjustment on top of close; BenchmarkPriceBar has no adjusted-level column at all. These are therefore split-adjusted price returns, dividends excluded -- not dividend-reinvested total returns. The abnormal return is a simple market-adjusted figure (stock return minus benchmark return, implicit beta of 1) -- it is not a CAPM alpha, a factor alpha, or a regression-based excess return.
